newsitem.title: JAPAN: Prudential Securities Japan says suspects fraud.
newsitem.headline: Prudential Securities Japan says suspects fraud.

text.p: Prudential Securities (Japan) Ltd Thursday confirmed reports it had asked Tokyo police to bring charges against a former executive it suspected of embezzling 2.2 billion yen ($20 million).
The company, a subsidiary of Prudential Securities Inc. of the United States, said the former executive had been pocketing shares entrusted to the firm by customers since around 1993.
It also suspected him of embezzling settlement money for share trading transactions. It had already purchased an equal amount of shares on the market and returned them to customers.

Charles Perkins, senior vice president in charge of public affairs at Prudential Securities Inc., said the loss had been wholly covered by an insurance policy and had not had any impact on the company's performance.
He said the former executive, who was laid off in May 1995 as part of a restructuring, admitted the wrongdoing to the company when it discovered the discrepancies in June.
Company officials declined to say if they knew the man's present whereabouts.
Prudential said it reported the loss to police in July 1995 and in April this year asked for legal action against the man.
The Japanese subsidiary's president, Takanori Hiramoto, said the man was not involved in any market trading while he was employed at the firm.

Prudential Securities (Japan) was licensed to operate in Japan in late 1979. It relinquished its membership of Tokyo Stock Exchange for trading Japanese shares in the spring of 1995, and its seat was sold to Smith New Court Securities (Japan) Ltd, a unit of Smith New Court Plc.
